sections.h2: What are my options for selling a house in Paterson fast?
sections.html:
A Paterson homeowner can list the house, sell it directly to a buyer, or accept a cash offer that skips repairs and showings. Paterson adds its own layers for vacant buildings, rent leveling and certificates of occupancy, so it pays to know which apply before you choose.

Paterson is the largest city in Passaic County and its county seat, with a 2025 Census Bureau estimate of 161,793 residents on 8.41 square miles of land. Only 26.9 percent of homes are owner-occupied, so many sellers own two- and three-family buildings or inherited a house from a relative. Start with this checklist:

  • Confirm whether the property counts as vacant, which triggers a city registration.
  • Find out if tenants live there and whether the building is covered by the rent leveling ordinance.
  • Collect the deed, the payoff figure and any code violation notices.
  • Ask the Division of Community Improvements what inspection a change of occupancy needs.

sections.h2: What is Paterson like for people selling a home?
sections.html:
Paterson was founded in 1791 by the Society for Establishing Useful Manufactures, which wanted to run mills off the Great Falls of the Passaic River. The first plans came from Pierre L'Enfant. The city grew into Silk City in the 19th century, and after a fire in 1902 downtown was rebuilt with four to seven story Beaux-Arts buildings, including City Hall from 1894. Today the Great Falls are part of the national park system, and the Paterson Museum sits in the Great Falls Historic District.

Parks include Eastside, Westside and Pennington Parks, and Lambert Castle, built in 1892 for a silk mill owner, is a local landmark. Neighborhoods vary a good deal. The Eastside and the Manor Section are in the 3rd Ward, Hillcrest is a largely residential area west of downtown, Lakeview sits in the south near the farmers market, and People's Park centers on Twenty-First Avenue. South Paterson is home to large Turkish and Arab communities.

Interstate 80 runs through the city, and State Routes 4, 19 and 20 serve it, with the Garden State Parkway crossing the south end. NJ Transit's Main Line train at Paterson station goes to Hoboken Terminal with a connection at Secaucus Junction, and the Broadway Bus Terminal in downtown is the end of many bus lines. Paterson Public Schools operate 43 schools with 24,692 students in 2023-24.

In August 2011 Hurricane Irene sent the Passaic River up to levels unseen in about a century, displacing thousands of people and closing river bridges. Anyone selling a riverside house should prepare an honest flood answer for the buyer.

sections.h2: Which Paterson city rules should a seller know?
sections.html:
The city enforces the New Jersey Uniform Construction Code through building, electrical, plumbing and fire inspectors, who issue permits and final approvals including Certificates of Occupancy and Continued Certificates of Occupancy. The Division of Community Improvements handles inspections, licenses, permits and certificates of occupancy, and its office hours are Monday through Friday from 8:30 to 4:30. Call 973-321-1232 for the current requirements on a sale.

  • Vacant buildings: an owner must register a vacant building within 30 days of it becoming vacant or of taking ownership, and the annual registration fee is $2,000. The owner names a local agent aged 21 or older who can be reached at all hours.
  • Foreclosed property: a creditor must register within seven days of starting foreclosure, at $500 a year.
  • Sold or transferred property: once a vacant property is sold or transferred, the owner gives the city proof within 30 days.
  • Rent leveling: owners of covered rentals submit an annual property registration form under Chapter 381 of the municipal code, at no fee, within 30 days of receiving it.

A property qualifies as abandoned in Paterson when it has been unoccupied six months and meets another test, such as unpaid taxes or a nuisance finding. Ask the Division of Community Improvements whether your house has been flagged before you sign a contract.

sections.h2: What state fees and forms apply when a Paterson house sells?
sections.html:
The State of New Jersey places the Realty Transfer Fee on the seller. A sale over $350,000 starts at $2.90 per $500 of price on the first $150,000, then moves to $4.25, $4.80, $5.30, $5.80 and finally $6.05 per $500 above $1,000,000. For prices at or below $350,000 the bracket rates are $2.00, $3.35 and $3.90 per $500. The Census median home value of $360,100 sits just above that $350,000 line, and your closing attorney can give you the exact dollar amount.

Sellers who qualify as senior citizens, or who are blind or disabled, pay lower brackets, and the exemption form is filed with the deed. Deeds that move a house from an estate to an heir are exempt. The GIT/REP form also goes with the deed, signed by whoever signs the deed, and helps the State decide whether a nonresident seller must prepay estimated income tax.

Since March 20, 2024, sellers must also disclose flood zone status and known flooding in the property condition disclosure statement before the buyer signs. The DEP offers a Flood Risk Notification Tool to help with the answers.

sections.h2: How can I appeal Paterson property taxes?
sections.html:
Paterson owners appeal at the Passaic County Board of Taxation, not at city hall. The petition must be received by April 1, or by May 1 in a year when the city completes a revaluation or reassessment.

The burden is on the owner to show the assessment is out of line with market value or with the district's common level range, which is 15 percent above or below the average ratio. Assessments above $1,000,000 can go directly to the State Tax Court, and a county board decision can be taken to the Tax Court within 45 days. Ask the Paterson tax collector for the current balance before you sign a contract.

faqs.q: Do I need to register my Paterson house if it is vacant?
faqs.a: Yes, if it meets the city's definition of a vacant building. The owner registers within 30 days and pays a $2,000 annual fee.

faqs.q: What is the city's rule on foreclosed properties?
faqs.a: A creditor that files a foreclosure complaint must register the property within seven days. The fee is $500 for the first year and for each renewal.

faqs.q: Who handles certificates of occupancy in Paterson?
faqs.a: The Division of Community Improvements, which enforces the Uniform Construction Code and issues certificates of occupancy. The office is open weekdays from 8:30 to 4:30.

faqs.q: Is the state transfer fee a seller cost in Paterson?
faqs.a: Yes. New Jersey charges the seller when the deed is recorded, in brackets that rise with the price.

faqs.q: When must a Paterson tax appeal be filed?
faqs.a: By April 1, or May 1 after a revaluation, with the Passaic County Board of Taxation.
